The frequency with which these clutches are produced varies, but field records from long-term nest-box studies indicate that a breeding pair typically rears between one and four clutches per year [F_R_i = between one and four clutches per year], with the upper limit observed during years of abundant insect prey linked to El Niño rainfall events. This reproductive strategy positions the species with a relatively high annual output for a small-bodied hirundine. The typical body temperature during active periods, when these metabolic and reproductive processes are sustained, is 41.6 °C [T = 41.6 °C], which reflects the elevated endothermic demands of sustained flight and diurnal foraging. The initial wet weight of a newly laid egg, measured immediately following oviposition in a controlled nest-box environment, was recorded at a mean of 1.3 grams [Ww0 = 1.3 grams], a value consistent with egg sizes reported for other Tachycineta species of similar adult dimensions. This small initial mass represents the starting point of a developmental trajectory that will see the embryo undergo rapid organogenesis and yolk absorption within the incubated shell.

Upon hatching, the altricial nestlings of Tachycineta stolzmanni emerge at a wet weight at birth of approximately 1.1 grams [Wwb = approximately 1.1 grams], a modest mass that underscores their extreme dependence on parental provisioning. This neonatal mass represents a slight reduction from the fresh egg weight, reflecting losses associated with metabolic activity during incubation and the shedding of the eggshell. The incubation period itself, during which the fertilised ovum develops into a cleavage-stage embryo and ultimately a hatching chick, is dependent on the thermal environment maintained by the incubating adult. Eggs incubated at a consistent temperature of 36 °C [T = 36 °C] hatch after a period of 16.5 days [ab = 16.5 days], although the literature reports a natural range of 15 to 18 days depending on microclimatic fluctuations within the nest cavity. This incubation duration is comparable to that of other Neotropical swallows and appears to be finely tuned to balance the trade-off between rapid embryonic development and the energetic costs of sustained brooding by the female. The relatively short interval from egg fertilisation to hatching is characteristic of many passerines adapted to seasonally predictable food resources.

Under the thermal conditions typical of the active adult songbird, where body temperature is maintained at 41.6 °C [T = 41.6 °C], the time since birth at fledging is 29 days [tx = 29 days], a duration consistent with the fledging ages reported for other Tachycineta species. Field observations confirm a range of 26 to 32 days for this milestone, with the variation attributable to differences in food delivery rates by the provisioning adults and ambient environmental temperatures. The capacity for first flight achievement marks a critical transition, as the fledgling shifts from a stationary, nest-dependent chick to a mobile juvenile capable of short foraging sorties. Initially, however, the fledgling remains reliant on parental provisioning for a period, as its flight feathers are not yet fully matured and its prey-capture skills are rudimentary. The relatively moderate duration of the nestling phase places Tachycineta stolzmanni among typical aerial insectivores, balancing the need for adequate feather growth and muscle development against the increasing predation risk associated with a prolonged stay in the nest.

Following the post-fledging period of parental independence and dietary transition, the juvenile birds undergo a period of physiological maturation that culminates in the attainment of reproductive maturity. Juveniles attain gonadal maturation, estimated from banding recaptures, at approximately 87 days since birth [tp = approximately 87 days since birth], a milestone that precedes first breeding at a temperature of 41.6 °C [T = 41.6 °C]by many months. This estimate aligns with data on gonadal swelling in first-year birds, which indicate that reproductive activation typically occurs within three months of fledging. However, the time since birth at first brood, marking the initiation of actual breeding, is considerably longer; field records indicate that individuals defer their first reproductive event until approximately 365 days since birth [tR = approximately 365 days since birth], a delay that allows young birds to develop high-quality plumage, establish a territory, and secure a mate within the often competitive aerial ins at a temperature of 41.6 °C [T = 41.6 °C]ectivore guild. This pattern of early gonadal maturation but delayed first clutch laying is common among temperate and tropical swallows, ensuring that first-time breeders invest in reproductive effort only when they have accrued sufficient foraging experience and physical condition to support the demands of incubation and nestling care.

Longevity records for Tachycineta stolzmanni, based on mark-recapture studies in stable populations along the Peruvian coast, indicate a maximum lifespan of approximately 9.1 years [am = approximately 9.1 years] when measured under the sustained active thermoregulatory conditions of 41.6 °C [T = 41.6 °C]. This lifespan is relatively substantial for a passerine of its size and is likely facilitated by a life-history strategy that emphasizes adult survival over high annual fecundity, as reflected in the species' moderate but repeatable clutch sizes. As adults, the birds attain a maximum adult body mass, or ultimate wet weight, of 16.5 grams [Wwi = 16.5 grams], placing them among the medium-sized members of the genus Tachycineta. This asymptotic mass is achieved by the end of the first year and is maintained through the adult life stage, buffered by fat reserves that are critical for surviving periods of diminished insect availability. The consistent multi-year lifespan, moderate body size, and a breeding strategy that spreads offspring across seasons together allow this species to persist in a habitat where rainfall and insect abundance are highly unpredictable from year to year.
